enzyme_name: Indole-3-glycerol phosphate lyase (indole synthase INS / tryptophan synthase alpha subunit TSA1; maize BX1)
organism_context: Reaction comes from an Arabidopsis model (DF_Athaliana). In plants the IGP-cleaving activity sits on a standalone subunit/paralogue (TSA1, INS, maize BX1); in bacteria TrpA and TrpB are separate chains in an alpha2beta2 complex (a complex, not a fused bifunctional enzyme). In fungi (Neurospora trp-3, yeast TRP5) the alpha and beta activities ARE fused on one polypeptide, which would be bifunctional in that lineage.
rationale: The chemistry (indole-3-glycerol phosphate -> indole + triose phosphate) is the indole-3-glycerol-phosphate lyase / tryptophan synthase alpha reaction; in the plant source organism it is run by a single-activity subunit or by the standalone indole synthase INS. Only the fungal fused alpha-beta chain would qualify as bifunctional.
direction_note: The triose product is mis-mapped: cpd16494 is sn-glycerol 1-phosphate (C3H7O6P), not D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate, and the water product is missing, patched with 2 H+ (ModelSEED status CI:-2) - so the DeltaG that drove the reverse call is computed on the wrong molecule.

enzyme_name: Ascorbate peroxidase (cytosolic APX1/APX2)
organism_context: Plant cytosolic APX isoforms; C3H/APX bifunctionality demonstrated in vitro and now in vivo in Brachypodium distachyon and Populus. Chloroplastic/peroxisomal APX isoforms are not reported to carry the C3H activity, and classical class-I heme peroxidases are monofunctional.
rationale: The catalyst is a class-I heme ascorbate peroxidase that oxidises two ascorbate molecules to two monodehydroascorbate radicals per H2O2; CRISPR knockouts in Brachypodium and poplar give in vivo evidence that the same cytosolic polypeptide also runs genuine 4-coumarate 3-hydroxylase catalysis, a second catalytic (not moonlighting) activity.
direction_note: Peroxidase turnover is irreversible; the ModelSEED reverse call would have monodehydroascorbate radicals regenerating H2O2, which no enzyme does (MDHA disproportionates to ascorbate + dehydroascorbate). The equation also drops the two water products (status MI:H:-8/O:-2).

enzyme_name: Sterol C-22 desaturase (cytochrome P450 CYP710A)
organism_context: Plant microsomal P450 (Arabidopsis CYP710A1, tomato CYP710A11, maize CYP710A8). It works with a separate NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase polypeptide - a two-protein system, not a fused bifunctional chain.
rationale: Sitosterol -> stigmasterol is the C22 desaturation run by CYP710A, a single-activity cytochrome P450; its redox partner is a distinct protein, so the multi-subunit exclusion applies.
direction_note: The real reaction is O2-dependent (sterol + O2 + NAD(P)H -> 22-ene sterol + 2 H2O + NAD(P)+); writing it as a bare, mass-balanced NADP+ dehydrogenation removes the O2 that makes it irreversible and lets the DeltaG favour the (nonexistent) reductive direction.

enzyme_name: Biotin synthase (BioB)
organism_context: Radical SAM [4Fe-4S]/[2Fe-2S] homodimer; characterised in E. coli, conserved in plants (Arabidopsis BIO2).
rationale: 9-Mercaptodethiobiotin is the established, kinetically competent intermediate of the single BioB active site, formed by 5'-deoxyadenosyl radical abstraction at C9 of dethiobiotin and sulfur donation from the enzyme's own auxiliary cluster; one catalytic activity only.
direction_note: SAM, 5'-deoxyadenosine, methionine and the sacrificial [2Fe-2S] sulfur are all absent, with free elemental S standing in for the cluster sulfide; the irreversible SAM cleavage that fixes the direction is exactly what the equation deletes.

enzyme_name: None assigned - lactonization of cis-2-hydroxycinnamate (2-coumarinate) to coumarin; the enzymatic route in plants runs through COUMARIN SYNTHASE (COSY) on the CoA thioester, not the free acid
organism_context: Arabidopsis (DF_Athaliana model). COSY is a BAHD-family protein that performs trans-cis isomerization followed by lactonization on o-hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA thioesters; the free-acid lactonization written here proceeds partly spontaneously and is light-catalysed.
rationale: No enzyme is assigned to the free-acid cyclisation of 2-coumarinate to coumarin; Vanholme et al. show the conversion happens partially spontaneously and that the enzymatic (COSY) route uses the CoA thioester, so there is no mono/bi/poly answer for this entry.
direction_note: Lactonization releases water, which the equation omits (status MI:H:-1/O:-1, CI:1); with no enzyme at all the direction is set by the irreversible ring closure, not by enzymology.

enzyme_name: None assigned - lactonization of 3,4,6-trihydroxy-cis-cinnamate to esculetin; enzymatic counterpart is COUMARIN SYNTHASE (COSY) acting on the CoA thioester
organism_context: Arabidopsis (DF_Athaliana model). Recombinant COSY makes umbelliferone, esculetin and scopoletin from the corresponding o-hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA thioesters; the free-acid cyclisation is partly spontaneous and light-catalysed.
rationale: Same chemistry as rxn30941 with the 3,4,6-trihydroxy substrate giving esculetin; the free-acid lactonization carries no EC assignment and proceeds non-enzymatically, so functionality cannot honestly be called mono- or bifunctional.
direction_note: The water released on lactone formation is missing (status MI:H:-1/O:-1, CI:1), so the +45 to +89 kJ/mol used to call the reaction reverse is not the DeltaG of the real cyclisation.

enzyme_name: Sterol C-22 desaturase (cytochrome P450 CYP710A)
organism_context: Plant microsomal P450; the 24-epi-campesterol -> brassicasterol C22 desaturation is the CYP710A reaction on the C28 sterol, paralleling sitosterol -> stigmasterol. Its NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase partner is a separate polypeptide.
rationale: Single-activity cytochrome P450 sterol 22-desaturase; the second protein it requires is a distinct reductase, so the multi-subunit exclusion applies rather than bifunctionality.
direction_note: As in rxn30827, O2 and the two product waters are deleted and the reaction is written as a reversible NADP+ dehydrogenation, which is what lets eQuilibrator score the physiologically impossible reductive direction as favourable.

enzyme_name: Ribonucleoside-triphosphate reductase (class III anaerobic NrdD; class II NrdJ in other lineages)
organism_context: EcoCyc reaction RXN0-723 (E. coli NrdD). NrdD needs the separate activase NrdG to install its glycyl radical - two polypeptides, a complex rather than a fused bifunctional enzyme. Class Ia RNR (R1/R2) is likewise two chains and works at the diphosphate level.
rationale: CTP -> dCTP is the nucleoside-triphosphate-level ribonucleotide reduction run by class II/III RNRs; the catalytic polypeptide carries one activity, with radical generation delegated to a separate activase subunit.
direction_note: The external reductant (formate for NrdD, thioredoxin/NrdH for NrdJ) and the water product are both absent (status MI:O:-1); ribonucleotide reduction is irreversible, so the reverse call is an artefact of the missing redox partner.

enzyme_name: Ribonucleoside-triphosphate reductase (class III anaerobic NrdD; class II NrdJ in other lineages)
organism_context: EcoCyc reaction RXN0-724 (E. coli NrdD, UTP -> dUTP). NrdD plus its separate NrdG activase is a two-protein system, not a fused bifunctional chain.
rationale: Same single-activity ribonucleotide reductase chemistry as rxn30989 on the uridine nucleotide; no second catalytic activity on the polypeptide.
direction_note: Reductant and water product stripped (status MI:O:-1); the 2'-deoxygenation is irreversible in vivo.

enzyme_name: Ribonucleoside-triphosphate reductase (class III anaerobic NrdD; class II NrdJ in other lineages)
organism_context: EcoCyc reaction RXN0-745 (E. coli NrdD, ATP -> dATP). NrdD/NrdG are separate polypeptides.
rationale: Single-activity ribonucleotide reductase acting at the triphosphate level; allosteric specificity and activity sites are regulatory, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Reductant and water product stripped (status MI:O:-1); dNTP formation never runs backwards.

enzyme_name: Ribonucleoside-triphosphate reductase (class III anaerobic NrdD; class II NrdJ in other lineages)
organism_context: EcoCyc reaction RXN0-746 (E. coli NrdD, GTP -> dGTP). NrdD/NrdG are separate polypeptides.
rationale: Same single-activity NTP-level ribonucleotide reduction as the other three RXN0-72x/74x entries.
direction_note: Reductant and water product stripped (status MI:O:-1), removing the irreversibility that fixes the forward direction.

enzyme_name: Thymidine kinase (TK1/tdk)
organism_context: Cellular (plant/bacterial/human) thymidine kinases are single-activity. Herpesviral TKs are the exception: HSV-1 TK and HHV-8 ORF21 carry both thymidine kinase and thymidylate kinase activity on one chain, i.e. genuinely bifunctional in that viral lineage.
rationale: The substrate pair (ATP + thymidine) identifies thymidine kinase; cellular TK1-type enzymes have one catalytic activity, and the dual TK/TMP-kinase chain is restricted to herpesviruses.
direction_note: The product is mis-mapped to thiamine phosphate (cpd00793) instead of thymidine 5'-monophosphate, a 2C/2N/1S error (status MI:C:2/H:2/N:2/O:-4/S:1); ATP-driven phosphoryl transfer is effectively irreversible forward regardless of what the bogus DeltaG says.

enzyme_name: Heme O synthase / protoheme IX farnesyltransferase (COX10, CyoE/CtaB)
organism_context: Polytopic inner-membrane/mitochondrial-inner-membrane prenyltransferase of the UbiA superfamily; COX10 in eukaryotes, CyoE/CtaB in bacteria.
rationale: A single intramembrane prenyl-transfer activity (EC 2.5.1.141) that farnesylates the C2 vinyl of heme B; its role in cytochrome oxidase assembly is a pathway role, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Both co-substrates (farnesyl diphosphate, H2O) and the diphosphate product are missing - KEGG R07411 is Heme + H2O + FPP <=> Heme O + PPi, while ModelSEED has only Heme <=> Heme O (status MI:C:15/H:26/O:1); PPi release is what makes the prenyl transfer irreversible.

enzyme_name: Oxaloacetate (enol form) decarboxylase - EC left at 4.1.1.- by KEGG R00219; enol-oxaloacetate decarboxylation is largely spontaneous/metal-catalysed
organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) via KEGG R00219. The named oxaloacetate decarboxylases are either a soluble Mg2+-dependent single-activity enzyme (EC 4.1.1.3) or the Na+-pumping OadABC membrane complex - separate polypeptides, so the complex exclusion applies there.
rationale: KEGG assigns no EC beyond 4.1.1.- to the enol-oxaloacetate (2-hydroxyethylenedicarboxylate) decarboxylation, and the uncatalysed reaction is fast, so the catalysing protein for this specific entry cannot be identified.
direction_note: cpd00204 is carbon monoxide (KEGG C00237), not the CO2 (C00011) of KEGG R00219 - status MI:O:-1 - so the DeltaG that produced the carboxylating reverse call is computed on the wrong product; decarboxylation of oxaloacetate is strongly downhill and carboxylation of pyruvate requires ATP or PEP.

enzyme_name: None - KEGG flags R01652 as spontaneous decarboxylation of 2-isopropyl-3-oxosuccinate following 3-isopropylmalate dehydrogenase (LeuB, EC 1.1.1.85)
organism_context: Leucine biosynthesis; soybean model (iRS1563) via KEGG R01652. The oxidative step before it is run by monofunctional 3-isopropylmalate dehydrogenase.
rationale: KEGG's own COMMENT reads 'spontaneous (following EC 1.1.1.85 or R04426 reaction)' - the beta-keto acid decarboxylates without a catalyst, so there is no enzyme to classify.
direction_note: KEGG disowns the step as non-enzymatic, and ModelSEED additionally writes the product as CO (cpd00204) rather than CO2 (status MI:O:-1); spontaneous beta-keto decarboxylation runs only toward 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoate.

enzyme_name: 3-Hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase (HMGR, EC 1.1.1.34)
organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563): plant class-I HMGR is a single-activity reductase (its membrane sterol-sensing anchor is regulatory, not catalytic - a moonlighting-type role that is excluded). In Enterococcus faecalis and related Gram-positives the orthologue MvaE is a genuinely fused dual-function acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase/HMG-CoA reductase polypeptide, i.e. bifunctional in that lineage.
rationale: The plant/animal enzyme carries only the NADPH-dependent four-electron reduction of HMG-CoA to mevalonate; the bifunctional thiolase/reductase fusion is a bacterial variant (Hedl et al.).
direction_note: The stoichiometry is garbled - 9 HMG-CoA and 9 CoA against 2 mevalonate, 2 NADPH and 27 H+ (status MI:C:-42/H:-70/O:-28, CI:-18) - so the ~640-1263 kJ/mol used to call it reverse is meaningless; HMGR is the committed, physiologically irreversible step toward mevalonate.

enzyme_name: zeta-Carotene desaturase (ZDS/CrtQ in plants and cyanobacteria; CrtI-type phytoene desaturase in bacteria and fungi)
organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) - plant plastid ZDS, a single FAD-dependent desaturase that passes electrons to plastoquinone. Bacterial/fungal CrtI performs three or four successive desaturations, but these are iterations of the same activity, not distinct catalytic activities.
rationale: Purified higher-plant zeta-carotene desaturase carries out the zeta-carotene -> neurosporene -> lycopene desaturations as one activity with a quinone/O2 acceptor; iterative turnover is not polyfunctionality.
direction_note: KEGG R04798 is zeta-carotene + reduced acceptor + O2 <=> neurosporene + 2 H2O + acceptor; ModelSEED replaces the acceptor/O2 couple with free H2, deleting the oxidative driving force that makes desaturation irreversible.

enzyme_name: None assigned - KEGG R04885 leaves the EC at 4.1.1.-; in eumelanogenesis 5,6-dihydroxyindole arises by spontaneous decarboxylative rearrangement of dopachrome, while dopachrome tautomerase (DCT/TYRP2) diverts the flux to DHICA instead
organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) via KEGG R04885. Dopachrome tautomerase, the one characterised enzyme on this branch, is a monofunctional binuclear-copper/zinc tyrosinase-family protein - but it makes DHICA, not the DHI written here.
rationale: No enzyme is assigned to decarboxylation of leucodopachrome (cyclodopa) to DHI; the comparable step in melanin synthesis is the spontaneous decarboxylative tautomerization of dopachrome, so the catalysing protein for this entry cannot be named.
direction_note: cpd00204 is carbon monoxide, not the CO2 of KEGG R04885 (status MI:H:-1/O:-1, CI:2); loss of CO2 with aromatization is irreversible either way.

enzyme_name: None assigned - decarboxylation of bis(4-chlorophenyl)acetate (DDA) to bis(4-chlorophenyl)methane (DDM) in DDT catabolism; KEGG R05376 leaves the EC at 4.1.1.-
organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) via KEGG R05376, a DDT-degradation step with no characterised protein; DDA is normally reported as a terminal DDT metabolite rather than as a substrate of a named decarboxylase.
rationale: No decarboxylase has been assigned to this step in the literature or in KEGG, so neither the protein nor its functionality can be established.
direction_note: cpd00204 is carbon monoxide rather than the CO2 of KEGG R05376 (status MI:H:2/O:-1, CI:2); the dGPredictor +46 kJ/mol behind the reverse call is therefore for the wrong reaction.

enzyme_name: Isoflavone 7-O-glucoside beta-glucosidase (isoflavone conjugate-hydrolysing beta-glucosidase, GH1/GH3)
organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563); the apoplast-localised soybean ICHG hydrolyses isoflavone 7-O-glucosides such as ononin and daidzin to the aglycones. KEGG's COMMENT on R07733 reads 'isoflavone glucoside glucosidase'.
rationale: A single-activity retaining glycoside hydrolase removing the 7-O-glucose from ononin to give formononetin; glycoside hydrolases of this family carry one catalytic activity (broad substrate tolerance is not bifunctionality).
direction_note: Both the water substrate and the glucose product are absent and the stoichiometry is garbled (8 ononin against 11 formononetin + 11 H+; status MI:H:-44/O:-28), so the ~614-1097 kJ/mol driving the reverse call is not the DeltaG of a glucoside hydrolysis - which is irreversible in the hydrolytic direction.

enzyme_name: Phytoene synthase (PSY/CrtB, EC 2.5.1.32)
organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) - plant plastid PSY is a standalone single-activity synthase. In many fungi the orthologue is a fused bifunctional phytoene synthase/lycopene cyclase on one chain (Xanthophyllomyces/Phaffia CrtYB, Rhodosporidium crtYB, Neurospora AL-2), which would be bifunctional in that lineage.
rationale: PSY condenses two GGPP via prephytoene diphosphate to 15-cis-phytoene; the two chemical steps run in one active site and are a single activity, whereas the fungal CrtYB fusion adds a genuinely separate cyclase activity.
direction_note: Both diphosphate products are missing (status MI:H:-2/O:-14/P:-4, CI:6), which is what inflates DeltaG to ~885 kJ/mol and flips the call; PPi release makes prenyl condensation irreversible. KEGG also tags R07916 'multistep reaction (see R02065+R07270)', but both steps belong to the one PSY polypeptide.

enzyme_name: None firmly assigned - aromatization of 2-fluoro-cis,cis-1,2-dihydroxycyclohexa-3,5-diene-1-carboxylate to catechol with loss of CO2 and fluoride; the upstream 2-halobenzoate 1,2-dioxygenase is a multi-component oxygenase/reductase system and KEGG leaves R08122 at EC 1.3.1.-
organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) via KEGG's fluorobenzoate degradation map; the characterised bacterial 2-halobenzoate 1,2-dioxygenases of Pseudomonas cepacia 2CBS and P. aeruginosa 142 are two- or three-component systems (separate oxygenase and reductase polypeptides), so the complex exclusion applies to them in any case.
rationale: The dihydrodiol-carboxylate produced by halobenzoate dioxygenation eliminates CO2 and halide to catechol spontaneously or via an unassigned dehydrogenase; no single protein can be named for this entry.
direction_note: CO2 and fluoride are both absent and the stoichiometry is garbled (6 diol-carboxylate against 7 catechol; status MI:F:-6/O:-10); aromatization with CO2 and HF loss is irreversible.

enzyme_name: 1,4-Dihydroxy-6-naphthoate synthase (MqnD; also called 5,8-dihydroxy-2-naphthoate synthase, EC 4.1.99.29)
organism_context: Futalosine/modified-futalosine pathway to menaquinone in Helicobacter, Campylobacter, Streptomyces and Thermus; the entry reaches the soybean model (iRS1563) through KEGG R08589.
rationale: MqnD performs the single retro-aldol/aromatization step converting cyclic dehypoxanthine futalosine to the dihydroxynaphthoate with release of dihydroxyacetone; one catalytic activity on one chain.
direction_note: The dihydroxyacetone (glycerone) co-product is dropped and the stoichiometry is garbled (12 substrate against 14 product + 25 H+; status MI:C:-14/H:-33/O:-28, CI:23), so the ~753-1387 kJ/mol behind the reverse call is not this reaction's DeltaG; aromatization makes it irreversible forward.

enzyme_name: No single enzyme - lumped photosynthetic linear electron flow (photosystem II, cytochrome b6f, photosystem I, ferredoxin and ferredoxin-NADP+ reductase)
organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) thylakoid light reaction; each participating photosystem is itself a many-subunit pigment-protein complex, so even per complex the multi-subunit exclusion applies.
rationale: Water oxidation to O2, transthylakoid proton translocation and NADP+ reduction are carried out by four separate membrane complexes driven by photons; no single polypeptide catalyses the written reaction, so no mono/bi/poly call is possible.
direction_note: The equation is mass-balanced but omits its energy source - light - so the +90 to +108 kJ/mol all three thermodynamic sources report is exactly the photon input, and reading that as 'reverse' would have the chloroplast consuming O2 and NADPH to make water.

enzyme_name: No single enzyme - model lump for triacylglycerol assembly, which in vivo runs on acyl-CoA via GPAT, LPAAT, phosphatidate phosphatase and acyl-CoA:diacylglycerol acyltransferase (DGAT); direct esterification of free palmitate with glycerol is only a lipase reaction run in reverse
organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) storage-lipid pseudo-reaction; DGAT, the committed step of the real route, is a monofunctional membrane acyltransferase but it acylates diacylglycerol with palmitoyl-CoA, not glycerol with free palmitate.
rationale: Four distinct acyltransferase/phosphatase steps on CoA thioesters are collapsed into one condensation of free fatty acid with glycerol, so no single enzyme catalyses the equation as written.
direction_note: Only one palmitate is written for a tri-palmitoyl product (status MI:C:32/H:65/O:4, CI:1), which is what produces dGPredictor's +496 kJ/mol and the reverse call; net flux in an oilseed is toward triacylglycerol, but note that the only enzyme that really acts on this substrate set, a lipase, would run the hydrolytic direction ModelSEED chose.
